claims.text: Traditional EAM references underrepresent the range of atomic configurations present in the ab initio liquid.
Underrepresentation by EAM references leads to poor reference–target phase-space overlap.
Poor phase-space overlap causes mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
An ML potential trained on ab initio configurations spanning solid and liquid states can reproduce the ab initio potential-energy landscape across diverse atomic configurations.
Training on an extensive and diverse ab initio dataset enables an ML potential to model complex interatomic interactions and diverse local environments accurately.
The ML potential will represent solid and liquid configurations better than traditional EAM potentials.
Improved representation of diverse configurations will enhance reference–target phase-space overlap relative to EAM references.
Enhanced reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
Using the ML reference may improve free-energy convergence and accuracy by approximately 20–30% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The proposed method applies to high-entropy alloys containing five or more metallic components in nearly equiatomic proportions.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.05 times the alloy melting temperature.
The proposed method covers both solid and liquid states near the melting point.
Performance may deteriorate in regions of configuration space that are poorly sampled by the training dataset.
The ML approach may involve computational-efficiency trade-offs.
A reduction of at least 20% in integration-path mismatch is the proposed threshold for a statistically significant improvement.
Failure of the ML reference to improve phase-space overlap and integration-path mismatch relative to EAM under identical conditions would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of ML-reference free energies to converge more closely to direct ab initio benchmark values than EAM-reference free energies would falsify the hypothesis.
